title: PriceUpdate
description: The approved, live shelf price. Published to retail/price/{product_id} by dashboard-api and by nothing else — the pricing agent publishes proposals, never prices. QoS 1, retained, so an edge node that reboots immediately receives the current price. Every message here represents a decision a human either made or delegated by policy.

product_id.description: Must equal the {product_id} segment of the topic it is published on.

price.description: The live price. Two decimal places. Consumers must parse as decimal, never float.

decision_id.description: The proposal this price came from, and the join key to its ExplainVector and audit row. NULL when a manager set the price with no agent proposal behind it — in that case there is no explanation to show, and the UI must say so rather than display a stale one.

reason_tag.description: Rendered verbatim on LCD line 2 of a 16x2 character display, so the 16 character limit is a hardware constraint, not a style preference. On an override this describes the manager's reason, not the agent's. May be empty ("") when a manager sets a price and gives no reason: the label then shows the price alone.

approval.description: How this price was authorized. 'auto' — inside the product's policy, applied without a human. 'manager' — a human approved the agent's proposed price as-is. 'override' — a human set a different price; `price` will NOT equal the proposal's proposed_price, so any explanation attached to decision_id explains what the agent WANTED, not what shipped. Consumers must not present it as explaining this price.

approved_by.description: Username of the deciding manager, or the literal 'policy' when approval is 'auto'.

agent_version.description: Carried through from the originating proposal. NULL for a manager-originated price.

ts.description: UTC ISO-8601. The moment of approval, not of the original proposal.
